scientific_context: Physiological disorder caused by localized calcium deficiency
pathogen_type: Physiological disorder (not caused by a pathogen)
description: Blossom end rot is a physiological disorder that affects watermelon and other fruiting vegetables. It is caused by insufficient calcium reaching developing fruit tissues, usually due to irregular watering, drought stress, high salinity, or excessive nitrogen fertilization. The disorder results in dark, sunken lesions at the blossom end of the fruit.
symptoms: water-soaked spot at blossom end of fruit
light tan lesion that enlarges over time
dark brown or black sunken area on fruit
leathery or dry tissue at blossom end
secondary soft rot when fungi or bacteria invade
affected fruit ripen earlier than normal
visual_signature: dark black patch at blossom end of watermelon
sunken leathery lesion on fruit tip
dry black rot on blossom end
discolored depressed area on fruit surface
spread: caused by environmental and nutritional imbalance
nutritional_management: apply agricultural lime to adjust soil pH
use calcium nitrate or calcium chloride foliar sprays when needed
cultural_control: proper plant spacing for air circulation
